data.cultural_impact: The name "Gavra" holds a significant cultural impact, as it is derived from the Greek language. In Greek mythology, Gavra was regarded as a goddess of bearing heavy burdens. This reflects the essence of the name, which can be translated to "heavy," "burden," or "weight." The cultural significance of the name can be seen in its meaning, as it represents strength, endurance, and the ability to carry a great load.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christendom, the name "Gavra" holds a profound spiritual significance. In the New Testament, the disciple Simon of Cyrene is also referred to as "Gavras" in some texts. According to the biblical account, when Jesus was carrying the Cross to Calvary, Simon was compelled by the Roman soldiers to help Him. This act of bearing the weight of the Cross symbolizes the spiritual burden that each believer carries in their own lives. As believers, we are called to carry our crosses and follow in the footsteps of Christ, denying ourselves and taking up our crosses daily. The name "Gavra" serves as a reminder of the strength and courage required to bear the spiritual weight of our own lives and the lives of those around us. In essence, the name "Gavra" encapsulates the Christian virtues of selflessness, endurance, and perseverance.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Gavra was a 5th century bishop in the Balkans. The name Gavra carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
